text: In the rain-dark meeting room above Marrowgate’s sluice house, the Water Board on Tuesday confirmed that Henrik Dalloway will continue as its chair, a post he has held since the winter floods of 2021. Dalloway, a former canal engineer turned civic administrator, was re-elected by a unanimous vote after a brief review of the board’s dredging programme and reservoir repairs. Founded in 1898 to manage the town’s springworks and later expanded after the 1967 basin collapse, the board remains one of Marrowgate’s quietest but most consequential institutions. Residents along the lower quay, still mindful of last summer’s restrictions, welcomed the announcement with cautious approval, noting that Dalloway has kept water tariffs unusually steady.
